messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — our Next.js middleware started throwing in prod after upgrading to the new JS SDK. 502 at the middleware entry, stack shows "setInterval is not defined". anyone else?

sam: yup saw this in staging. reproduced with a minimal middleware that imports the SDK at module top-level. error during cold start.

maria: stack snippet:```
Error: setInterval is not defined
    at Object.<anonymous> (/var/task/_middleware.js:12:7)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:999:30)
```

ben: root cause: SDK spawns a background token refresher at module initialization (uses setInterval) — that doesn't fly in Vercel Edge/Next middleware which runs in a service-worker-like runtime without Node timers during module init.

nina: also ran into TS issues when trying to import the SDK in edge functions — tsc complains about Node types (Buffer/NodeJS namespace) leaking into the SDK typings. dev experience is rough.

ben: quick workaround for apps: avoid importing SDK at top-level. dynamic import inside the middleware handler and opt out of background refresh. e.g.```js
export default async function middleware(req) {
  const { RedwoodClient } = await import('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({
    auth: { enableBackgroundRefresh: false } // opt-out for edge
  });
  // do a sync refresh/check inside the request path if needed
}
```

maria: that unblock helped us get a patch live. but it's awkward to require dynamic import and per-request refresh for everyone.

jess: FYI I opened a fix branch in the SDK that guards timer usage and falls back to a request-driven refresh when timers are unavailable. also added a small runtime-detect helper: isEdgeRuntime() -> checks for typeof process === 'undefined' && typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function' etc. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412

nina: for the typings I proposed we ship an edge-friendly d.ts entrypoint that avoids Node-specific types (no Buffer/Stream references) and uses DOM libs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/413 — this should stop tsc from complaining for edge targets.

sam: thanks. can we get a patch release? this broke a couple of onboarding sample apps and some customers using Next middleware.

jess: cutting 0.11.2-rc1 with the timer guard + typing tweaks now. will add a short migration note: if you rely on background refresh, set enableBackgroundRefresh: false and call client.refreshTokenIfNeeded(req) inside middleware.

infra-bot: deploy queued: build-sdk-0.11.2-rc1 -> staging (job 7890).

deploy-bot: build succeeded, staging deploy started (staging-redwood-sdk).

maria: will try rc1 in staging and report back. thanks for quick turnaround :rocket: 

ben: follow-up item: add unit tests that run the SDK in a simulated service-worker-like environment (no timers, no process). otherwise this will pop up again.

jess: added tests + CI matrix entry. merging once CI green. linking to issue #289 (edge runtime CI matrix).

maria: great. leaving a note in the sample-app readme to avoid top-level imports until rc is in stable.

sam: tip for others: if you hit mysterious build failures with imports like "error: cannot resolve 'fs'" when importing the SDK, check tree-shaking: make sure bundler uses the ESM entrypoint or use dynamic import. SDK team: maybe publish a dedicated "edge" entrypoint in package.json exports?

jess: agreed — package.json exports now include an "edge" entry that points to a tiny shim (guards + types) so bundlers can pick it up. that should smooth out ESM/CJS interop and reduce fs/Node leakage.

maria: awesome. thanks everyone — will post a short note on the onboarding docs and mark the sample app repos with the workaround.

sam: good followups: add migration snippet to the release notes and update the Next middleware example in /examples.

maria: closing the loop once staging verifies.
